_comment: Frozen table of the kinds of memory a room keeps, and what a write from the
memory route (the app's editor, `memory set`, an agent, a scenario) may do to
each. A key's kind is the first whose pattern matches it (`*` is one part of
a key, `**` any number of parts). The hub checks every write from that route
against its kind before anything is saved (fastapi-backend/app/services/
memory_kinds.py, called from routes/memory.py's upsert), so every writer
there gets the same refusal: {error: <code>, message, key}. The hub's own
processes (the conductor, the synthesizer, leases, uploads) write through
their own routes and own what this table keeps from people. `edit`: what a
person may write (`body`, `field` for a body drawn from `source`, or
`none`). `fixed`: frontmatter a person may not change. `checks`: what's run
on the written content. The frontend's copy (mycelium-frontend/src/lib/
memory-kinds.ts) says which kinds its editor offers. Asserted by

kinds.says: An upload is its file, and can't be edited. Upload the file again to replace it.
Mycelium writes this after every step of a flow, so it can't be edited.
This is the record of a flow's run, written as it runs, so it can't be edited.
